task-intent.statement: A closeout presenting the epic as finished, with three sites that could not be swept recorded as a documented limit of the door's isolation property.

expected-behavior.statement: The human would accept the limit as the honest boundary of the work.

observed-behavior.statement: He rejected the framing: an exception to the single access point is a failure rather than a limit, and a second door would be an acceptable answer where a surviving CLI path for agents is not. Scope was added after the epic had been declared complete, and the spine's execute step was reopened because a spine claiming the run had ended would have been false.

impact-cost.statement: A closeout was withdrawn and a third wave ran. The four closeout gates already attested cascaded back to pending, and the hygiene half genuinely had to be redone over new branches and worktrees.

workaround.statement: The reopen was recorded rather than worked around, and it became the clearest evidence for the very issue it enabled -- the run's own plan changed mid-flight and the engine's only way to express that was to unfreeze a frozen middle.

task-intent.statement: An issue asserting that a role's authored gates could not live in its own spine because a gated plan cannot grow.

expected-behavior.statement: The remaining work would be building a mutable middle.

observed-behavior.statement: Both halves of the premise were wrong. amend() already gave a gated plan add/drop/rescope with reason and authority recorded, exposed at the door. What was missing was the freeze: _floor() protected only what had already been started, so a plan's opening was covered by accident of status and its closing by nothing. A single unforced call dropped a Commander's own review, feedback and archive, exit 0.

impact-cost.statement: The issue as filed would have funded building a capability that already shipped, while leaving the actual hole open.

workaround.statement: The lane reconciled against the code before planning, as delegated-mode doctrine requires, and the problem shrank from a design question to a declaration plus one guard.

task-intent.statement: A declaration form chosen for the bookend freeze, with the human picking per-gate flags over a single declared region.

expected-behavior.statement: The chosen form's silent-permissive failure mode would surface eventually, mitigated by a lint.

observed-behavior.statement: It surfaced within minutes of the merge, on the first spine minted afterwards. init_work_area.py mints from the installed corpus, which predated the merge, so the repo carried two declarations and the installed copy carried none -- and the new spine came out undeclared with nothing saying so. The freeze protects nothing until the corpus is reinstalled.

impact-cost.statement: No run was harmed, but the mechanism was inert at the moment it was believed to be protecting runs, and only an unrelated check caught it.

workaround.statement: The lint was promoted from a deferred candidate to part of the same wave, and scoped to catch repo-versus-installed drift as well as a missing declaration, because the second is how the first happens.

task-intent.statement: A crew needing a check waived that it is forbidden to waive itself, escalating to its parent as the engine instructs.

observed-behavior.statement: The parent could not: the engine refuses an action on a checklist an active session owns, and the two routes its refusal names are both defects this epic filed -- passing the child's session id is impersonation, and a forced claim erases actor attribution. The working sequence is release, parent claims, parent waives, parent releases, child reclaims, and it is written down nowhere. Two lanes hit it in one wave.

impact-cost.statement: Two round trips between parent and child, and a recovery that existed only in the messages the two exchanged.

workaround.statement: The handshake was performed by hand both times and staged as a candidate on the second occurrence, with the recurrence stated, because one occurrence reads as bad luck and two in a wave is a mechanism.

task-intent.statement: A diagnosis, filed as an issue, that a launcher inherited the host's model default when the flag was unset.

expected-behavior.statement: The lane dispatched to fix it would build against that diagnosis.

observed-behavior.statement: The launcher refuses a dispatch with no model rather than inheriting one, and had done so since an earlier issue closed that exact failure mode. The escalation came instead from a Commander writing a tier into an unconstrained free-text field in its own handoff, with reasons. Two populations had been measured -- bare helper launches, which do inherit, and launcher dispatches, which refuse -- and written up as one story.

impact-cost.statement: A filed issue carried a false mechanism until the lane reading the code found it. The remedy was unaffected, but anyone building from the issue body would have built against a defect that did not exist.

workaround.statement: Corrected publicly on the issue as a comment rather than by a silent edit, so the wrong diagnosis stays visible beside the right one, and the lane restated it in its own return.
